assumptions_metadata.task_description: Compute weekly dropout-risk scores and financial-aid eligibility flags for current students using academic performance, admissions, and billing data.

assumptions_on_column_groups.target_column_group: Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled),Curricular units 1st sem (approved),Curricular units 1st sem (without evaluations),Curricular units 1st sem (grade)

assumptions.assumption: Curricular units 1st sem (grade) is between 0 and 20.
Curricular units 1st sem (approved) <= Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled).
Curricular units 1st sem (without evaluations) <= Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled).
If Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled) = 0 then Curricular units 1st sem (approved) = 0 and Curricular units 1st sem (grade) = 0.
Spearman correlation between Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled) and Curricular units 1st sem (approved) > 0.5.

assumptions_on_column_groups.target_column_group: Curricular units 2nd sem (enrolled),Curricular units 2nd sem (approved),Curricular units 2nd sem (without evaluations),Curricular units 2nd sem (grade)

assumptions.assumption: Curricular units 2nd sem (grade) is between 0 and 20.
Curricular units 2nd sem (approved) <= Curricular units 2nd sem (enrolled).
Curricular units 2nd sem (without evaluations) <= Curricular units 2nd sem (enrolled).
At least 90% of Curricular units 2nd sem (without evaluations) values are 0.
Spearman correlation between Curricular units 2nd sem (enrolled) and Curricular units 2nd sem (approved) > 0.5.

assumptions_on_column_groups.target_column_group: Debtor,Tuition fees up to date,Scholarship holder

assumptions.assumption: Debtor = 1 implies Tuition fees up to date = 0.
Tuition fees up to date = 1 implies Debtor = 0.
Among Scholarship holder = 1, at least 95% have Tuition fees up to date = 1.
Among Tuition fees up to date = 0, at least 90% have Debtor = 1.
Admission grade is between 0 and 200.
Previous qualification (grade) is between 0 and 200.
Pearson correlation between Previous qualification (grade) and Admission grade > 0.5.
International is binary in {0,1}.
International = 1 implies Nacionality != 1 (domestic code).
The share of International = 1 is <= 0.05.
Application order is an integer in [0, 9].
Value 1 appears in at least 60% of rows.
Value 0 appears in less than 0.1% of rows.

import argparse
import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--input', type=str, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--output', type=str, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()

input_csv = os.path.join(args.input, 'previous_data.csv')
output_dir = args.output
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

# Load data
 df = pd.read_csv(input_csv)

# Focus on current students for weekly scoring
current = df[df['Target'] == 'Enrolled'].copy()

# Column aliases for readability
s1_en = current['Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled)']
s1_ap = current['Curricular units 1st sem (approved)']
s1_wo = current['Curricular units 1st sem (without evaluations)']
s1_gr = current['Curricular units 1st sem (grade)']

s2_en = current['Curricular units 2nd sem (enrolled)']
s2_ap = current['Curricular units 2nd sem (approved)']
s2_wo = current['Curricular units 2nd sem (without evaluations)']
s2_gr = current['Curricular units 2nd sem (grade)']

admission = current['Admission grade']
prev_grade = current['Previous qualification (grade)']

intl = current['International']
nationality = current['Nacionality']

app_order = current['Application order']

debtor = current['Debtor']
tuition_ok = current['Tuition fees up to date']
sch = current['Scholarship holder']

# Academic range and relational constraints (1st sem)
# ASSERTION_START
assert ((s1_gr >= 0) & (s1_gr <= 20)).all()
assert (s1_ap <= s1_en).all()
assert (s1_wo <= s1_en).all()
mask_e0 = s1_en == 0
if mask_e0.any():
    assert (s1_ap[mask_e0] == 0).all()
    assert (s1_gr[mask_e0] == 0).all()
if len(s1_en) > 1:
    assert s1_en.corr(s1_ap, method='spearman') > 0.5
# ASSERTION_END

# Compute 1st sem features
s1_grade_norm = s1_gr / 20.0
s1_pass_rate = (s1_ap / s1_en.replace(0, np.nan)).fillna(0.0)
s1_eval_participation = (1.0 - (s1_wo / s1_en.replace(0, np.nan))).fillna(0.0)

# Academic range and relational constraints (2nd sem)
# ASSERTION_START
assert ((s2_gr >= 0) & (s2_gr <= 20)).all()
assert (s2_ap <= s2_en).all()
assert (s2_wo <= s2_en).all()
if len(s2_en) > 1:
    assert s2_en.corr(s2_ap, method='spearman') > 0.5
assert (s2_wo == 0).mean() >= 0.90
# ASSERTION_END

# Compute 2nd sem features
s2_grade_norm = s2_gr / 20.0
s2_pass_rate = (s2_ap / s2_en.replace(0, np.nan)).fillna(0.0)
s2_eval_participation = (1.0 - (s2_wo / s2_en.replace(0, np.nan))).fillna(0.0)

# Billing consistency and distributional checks for financial-aid logic
# ASSERTION_START
assert not ((debtor == 1) & (tuition_ok == 1)).any()
assert not ((tuition_ok == 1) & (debtor == 1)).any()
if len(debtor) > 0:
    assert debtor.mean() <= 0.20
mask_sch = sch == 1
if mask_sch.any():
    assert tuition_ok[mask_sch].mean() >= 0.95
mask_tuition_bad = tuition_ok == 0
if mask_tuition_bad.any():
    assert debtor[mask_tuition_bad].mean() >= 0.90
# ASSERTION_END

# Admissions and prior preparedness constraints
# ASSERTION_START
assert ((admission >= 0) & (admission <= 200)).all()
assert ((prev_grade >= 0) & (prev_grade <= 200)).all()
if len(current) > 1:
    assert admission.corr(prev_grade, method='pearson') > 0.5
# ASSERTION_END

# Internationality constraints
# ASSERTION_START
assert intl.isin([0, 1]).all()
assert not ((intl == 1) & (nationality == 1)).any()
if len(intl) > 0:
    assert intl.mean() <= 0.05
# ASSERTION_END

# Application order constraints used for cohort calibration
# ASSERTION_START
assert ((app_order >= 0) & (app_order <= 9)).all()
assert (app_order == app_order.astype(int)).all()
if len(app_order) > 0:
    assert (app_order == 1).mean() >= 0.60
    assert (app_order == 0).mean() < 0.001
# ASSERTION_END

# Build weekly dropout-risk score
perf_sem = (
    0.4 * (s1_grade_norm.add(s2_grade_norm).div(2)) +
    0.3 * (s1_pass_rate.add(s2_pass_rate).div(2)) +
    0.3 * (s1_eval_participation.add(s2_eval_participation).div(2))
)

admission_norm = admission / 200.0
prev_norm = prev_grade / 200.0
preparedness = (admission_norm + prev_norm) / 2.0

core_score = 0.7 * perf_sem + 0.3 * preparedness
base_risk = 1.0 - core_score

# Risk penalties/credits reflecting operational policies
billing_penalty = np.where((debtor == 1) | (tuition_ok == 0), 0.15, 0.0)
intl_penalty = np.where(intl == 1, 0.05, 0.0)
app_penalty = np.where(app_order == 1, -0.02, 0.03)
app_penalty = np.where(app_order == 0, 0.10, app_penalty)

risk = base_risk + billing_penalty + intl_penalty + app_penalty
risk = np.clip(risk, 0.0, 1.0)

# Financial-aid eligibility: emergency retention support
# Requires financial need plus sufficient academic trajectory
financial_need = ((debtor == 1) | (tuition_ok == 0)) & (sch == 0)
strong_trajectory = (perf_sem >= 0.45) | (preparedness >= 0.55)
high_risk = risk >= 0.55
aid_eligible = financial_need & (strong_trajectory | high_risk)

result = pd.DataFrame({
    'student_index': current.index,
    'dropout_risk': risk.round(4),
    'aid_eligible': aid_eligible.astype(bool)
})

result.to_csv(os.path.join(output_dir, 'weekly_dropout_risk_and_aid.csv'), index=False)

dataset_record.task_description: Compute weekly dropout-risk scores and financial-aid eligibility flags for current students using academic performance, admissions, and billing data.

assumptions.target_column_group: Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled),Curricular units 1st sem (approved),Curricular units 1st sem (without evaluations),Curricular units 1st sem (grade)

assumptions.assumption: Curricular units 1st sem (grade) is between 0 and 20.
Curricular units 1st sem (approved) <= Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled).
Curricular units 1st sem (without evaluations) <= Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled).
If Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled) = 0 then Curricular units 1st sem (approved) = 0 and Curricular units 1st sem (grade) = 0.
Spearman correlation between Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled) and Curricular units 1st sem (approved) > 0.5.

assumptions.target_column_group: Curricular units 2nd sem (enrolled),Curricular units 2nd sem (approved),Curricular units 2nd sem (without evaluations),Curricular units 2nd sem (grade)

assumptions.assumption: Curricular units 2nd sem (grade) is between 0 and 20.
Curricular units 2nd sem (approved) <= Curricular units 2nd sem (enrolled).
Curricular units 2nd sem (without evaluations) <= Curricular units 2nd sem (enrolled).
At least 90% of Curricular units 2nd sem (without evaluations) values are 0.
Spearman correlation between Curricular units 2nd sem (enrolled) and Curricular units 2nd sem (approved) > 0.5.

assumptions.target_column_group: Debtor,Tuition fees up to date,Scholarship holder

assumptions.assumption: Debtor = 1 implies Tuition fees up to date = 0.
Tuition fees up to date = 1 implies Debtor = 0.
Among Scholarship holder = 1, at least 95% have Tuition fees up to date = 1.
Among Tuition fees up to date = 0, at least 90% have Debtor = 1.
Admission grade is between 0 and 200.
Previous qualification (grade) is between 0 and 200.
Pearson correlation between Previous qualification (grade) and Admission grade > 0.5.
International is binary in {0,1}.
International = 1 implies Nacionality != 1 (domestic code).
The share of International = 1 is <= 0.05.
Application order is an integer in [0, 9].
Value 1 appears in at least 60% of rows.
Value 0 appears in less than 0.1% of rows.

dataset_record.code:
import argparse
import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--input', type=str, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--output', type=str, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()

input_csv = os.path.join(args.input, 'previous_data.csv')
output_dir = args.output
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

# Load data
 df = pd.read_csv(input_csv)

# Focus on current students for weekly scoring
current = df[df['Target'] == 'Enrolled'].copy()

# Column aliases for readability
s1_en = current['Curricular units 1st sem (enrolled)']
s1_ap = current['Curricular units 1st sem (approved)']
s1_wo = current['Curricular units 1st sem (without evaluations)']
s1_gr = current['Curricular units 1st sem (grade)']

s2_en = current['Curricular units 2nd sem (enrolled)']
s2_ap = current['Curricular units 2nd sem (approved)']
s2_wo = current['Curricular units 2nd sem (without evaluations)']
s2_gr = current['Curricular units 2nd sem (grade)']

admission = current['Admission grade']
prev_grade = current['Previous qualification (grade)']

intl = current['International']
nationality = current['Nacionality']

app_order = current['Application order']

debtor = current['Debtor']
tuition_ok = current['Tuition fees up to date']
sch = current['Scholarship holder']

# Academic range and relational constraints (1st sem)
# ASSERTION_START
assert ((s1_gr >= 0) & (s1_gr <= 20)).all()
assert (s1_ap <= s1_en).all()
assert (s1_wo <= s1_en).all()
mask_e0 = s1_en == 0
if mask_e0.any():
    assert (s1_ap[mask_e0] == 0).all()
    assert (s1_gr[mask_e0] == 0).all()
if len(s1_en) > 1:
    assert s1_en.corr(s1_ap, method='spearman') > 0.5
# ASSERTION_END

# Compute 1st sem features
s1_grade_norm = s1_gr / 20.0
s1_pass_rate = (s1_ap / s1_en.replace(0, np.nan)).fillna(0.0)
s1_eval_participation = (1.0 - (s1_wo / s1_en.replace(0, np.nan))).fillna(0.0)

# Academic range and relational constraints (2nd sem)
# ASSERTION_START
assert ((s2_gr >= 0) & (s2_gr <= 20)).all()
assert (s2_ap <= s2_en).all()
assert (s2_wo <= s2_en).all()
if len(s2_en) > 1:
    assert s2_en.corr(s2_ap, method='spearman') > 0.5
assert (s2_wo == 0).mean() >= 0.90
# ASSERTION_END

# Compute 2nd sem features
s2_grade_norm = s2_gr / 20.0
s2_pass_rate = (s2_ap / s2_en.replace(0, np.nan)).fillna(0.0)
s2_eval_participation = (1.0 - (s2_wo / s2_en.replace(0, np.nan))).fillna(0.0)

# Billing consistency and distributional checks for financial-aid logic
# ASSERTION_START
assert not ((debtor == 1) & (tuition_ok == 1)).any()
assert not ((tuition_ok == 1) & (debtor == 1)).any()
if len(debtor) > 0:
    assert debtor.mean() <= 0.20
mask_sch = sch == 1
if mask_sch.any():
    assert tuition_ok[mask_sch].mean() >= 0.95
mask_tuition_bad = tuition_ok == 0
if mask_tuition_bad.any():
    assert debtor[mask_tuition_bad].mean() >= 0.90
# ASSERTION_END

# Admissions and prior preparedness constraints
# ASSERTION_START
assert ((admission >= 0) & (admission <= 200)).all()
assert ((prev_grade >= 0) & (prev_grade <= 200)).all()
if len(current) > 1:
    assert admission.corr(prev_grade, method='pearson') > 0.5
# ASSERTION_END

# Internationality constraints
# ASSERTION_START
assert intl.isin([0, 1]).all()
assert not ((intl == 1) & (nationality == 1)).any()
if len(intl) > 0:
    assert intl.mean() <= 0.05
# ASSERTION_END

# Application order constraints used for cohort calibration
# ASSERTION_START
assert ((app_order >= 0) & (app_order <= 9)).all()
assert (app_order == app_order.astype(int)).all()
if len(app_order) > 0:
    assert (app_order == 1).mean() >= 0.60
    assert (app_order == 0).mean() < 0.001
# ASSERTION_END

# Build weekly dropout-risk score
perf_sem = (
    0.4 * (s1_grade_norm.add(s2_grade_norm).div(2)) +
    0.3 * (s1_pass_rate.add(s2_pass_rate).div(2)) +
    0.3 * (s1_eval_participation.add(s2_eval_participation).div(2))
)

admission_norm = admission / 200.0
prev_norm = prev_grade / 200.0
preparedness = (admission_norm + prev_norm) / 2.0

core_score = 0.7 * perf_sem + 0.3 * preparedness
base_risk = 1.0 - core_score

# Risk penalties/credits reflecting operational policies
billing_penalty = np.where((debtor == 1) | (tuition_ok == 0), 0.15, 0.0)
intl_penalty = np.where(intl == 1, 0.05, 0.0)
app_penalty = np.where(app_order == 1, -0.02, 0.03)
app_penalty = np.where(app_order == 0, 0.10, app_penalty)

risk = base_risk + billing_penalty + intl_penalty + app_penalty
risk = np.clip(risk, 0.0, 1.0)

# Financial-aid eligibility: emergency retention support
# Requires financial need plus sufficient academic trajectory
financial_need = ((debtor == 1) | (tuition_ok == 0)) & (sch == 0)
strong_trajectory = (perf_sem >= 0.45) | (preparedness >= 0.55)
high_risk = risk >= 0.55
aid_eligible = financial_need & (strong_trajectory | high_risk)

result = pd.DataFrame({
    'student_index': current.index,
    'dropout_risk': risk.round(4),
    'aid_eligible': aid_eligible.astype(bool)
})

result.to_csv(os.path.join(output_dir, 'weekly_dropout_risk_and_aid.csv'), index=False)
